lede: Florida State carries a full EdgeDesk team rating at +1.6; Central Arkansas is not one of the 138 FBS programmes EdgeDesk rates, so the comparison is one-sided by construction rather than by judgement.
EdgeDesk makes it Florida State -31.7 before any sportsbook number is consulted, with Florida State winning 98% of simulations.

The roster and position-group comparison below explains where EdgeDesk’s separation comes from on the side it can measure; Central Arkansas is absent from the FBS player dataset, so the exact size of that gap is not established.
Data confidence on this matchup is 45% — enough to publish, not enough to treat the exact margin as settled.

favourite.heading: Why Florida State can pull away
bullets: Florida State is the better football team by 27.7 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 64% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+27.7 pts).
Playing at Florida State is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Central Arkansas can keep it close
bullets: The outcome range is 15.1 points wide at one sigma — p10 +8.7 to p90 +52.7 for Florida State, so a projection of +31.7 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 3%.
60% of the model’s own input contract was empty for this game — no starter, injury, schedule or per-player talent context reached it, so the number leans on team strength more than it should.
Central Arkansas is not in the FBS rating set, so EdgeDesk cannot measure what it does well. An unmeasured opponent is an unknown, not a weak one, and the size of the gap is not established.
